newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Black merchant bank launches S.African equity fund.
newsitem.headline: Black merchant bank launches S.African equity fund.

text.p: Majority black-owned merchant and investment banking firm DLJ Pleiade announced on Thursday it had launched a one billion rand private equity fund known as the DLJ Pleiade Southern Africa Investors.

The firm, which was formed in November 1995, said in a statement the fund consisted of a 400 million rand private equity partnership designed to make equity investments in small to medium-sized unlisted companies.
It would be supplemented by 600 million rand in senior debt funding.
DLJ Pleiade is a joint venture between New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail) and leading U.S. investment and merchant bank Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette Inc.

DLJ Pleiade's other major shareholder is African Bank and it is South Africa's only independently operating black majority-owned domestic merchant banking firm with domestic and international expertise.

"The fund will be further supported by private equity funds managed by affiliates of Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. designed to seek long term capital appreciation by making investments in both developed and emerging markets," DLJ Pleiade said.
It said ten investors had made equity commitments of between 20 million rand and 100 million rand in the fund.
"Fund manager DLJ Pleiade has invested 50 million rand and the fund will be the exclusuve vehicle for the firm's investment banking activity".
The senior debt funding would be sourced through financial Services group NBS Holdings Ltd and the African Bank Ltd.
